items.reason: Pinning needs the GitHub API to resolve each tag to a commit SHA and this session has no network; the repo's own `npm run actions:pin` already does the whole close (it rewrites the workflows AND flips STRICT/RATCHET in scripts/actions-pin.mjs in the same pass), so the missing piece is one networked run, not tooling.

Added `npm run llm:budget:check` — a per-operation input-cost budget (system + prompt + JSON schema, all committed data) recorded in test-llm/budget.json, blocking inside check:ci, with a run-wide ceiling for uniform drift and a reason-required `--accept` to move a number.

Added `npm run context:decay` — it walks the real import graph against context-map.json's group boundaries; `--check` (blocking, in check:ci) fails a change that makes a mapped file import a feature group it did not import before unless the importing context declares it in cross_refs, and the census half prints what already crosses.

A mutation score cannot be asserted without executing the suite once per mutant, and this session has no test runner or shell execution; committing a threshold I could not measure would either be red on arrival or a number chosen to pass, which is the failure ADR-0007 names.

lessons: This repository states rung discipline as law (docs/adr/0007-gate-rung-discipline.md): a check may only BLOCK if it passes on the tree today, otherwise it reports against a committed ratchet. A gate landed with an unmeasured threshold is worse than no gate here, so an offline agent should prefer a diff-scoped rule (green by construction on an empty diff) over a tree-wide count it cannot baseline.

Cost/limit baselines for the LLM layer can be derived statically: test-llm/registry.mjs holds the system prompt, user prompt and schema of every operation as literal committed data, so what a golden run costs on the input side is computable with no model call, no network and no money — which is what lets a cost gate live inside check:ci rather than on the paid on-demand rung.

context-map.json's `cross_refs` field is an unused declaration surface: every context already lists the contexts it references, so a boundary rule can be enforced against a declaration the generator already emits instead of inventing a new config file.
